segments.caption: The video documents the early stages of a beehive's establishment in a tree. It begins with a shot of the tree on April 4, 2013, with text indicating "A swarm moved in." Subsequent frames show a close-up of the tree trunk, revealing a man-made opening that was created six days later, on April 10, 2013, as marked by the text "First opening." A hand is seen pointing to
A beekeeper examines the first opening of a new beehive, revealing a dense cluster of newly hatched bees emerging from their brood cells.

A close-up view shows a dense cluster of dark, crawling insects, likely a newly established bee colony, nestled within a wooden cavity. The scene is contextualized by a subsequent shot of a hand opening the tree cavity 17 days after the colony’s “birth,” revealing the same teeming mass of bees actively building and occupying their new home.

A beekeeper examines a thriving, densely packed honeybee colony emerging from a tree cavity, with a hand shown holding a rope tied to the tree stump, indicating the site of the hive’s “birth” 37 days prior.
A beekeeper inspects a large, active swarm of bees clustered inside a hollow tree, pointing to the cavity where the colony is nestled.

A person carefully removes a circular section of bark from a large tree trunk, revealing a dense swarm of bees nestled inside the hollow cavity, before extracting the bee-filled wood and leaving the tree cavity empty.
A close-up view reveals a dense swarm of bees actively moving across and clustering around exposed honeycomb structures within a hollow tree trunk, indicating a thriving, natural bee colony.
A hand gently probes a dense cluster of bees swarming over a honeycomb, revealing a dark, hollow cavity within the hive structure.
